ledger.claim: The GPS trace for TRP-00104 runs 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km, so the excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed — more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute — and the deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurement. It is the trace figure (34.17 km) that governs the threshold test, not the trip record's rounded 34.2 km convenience copy. The excess falls short of the 8.0 km and 50% material gates, but materiality goes to remedy, not to whether a deviation exists.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100.0%, the gaps array is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0, and the 10 second sample interval matches the 10 second expected interval, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. The excess may therefore be established on the gps_trace alone, and the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) and the escalation route in POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) are not open on this record.

The rider has discharged her initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the identifier TRP-00104 and the same 20:35:10 start, so POL-RD-08(a) is met; and the excess above exceeds the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace, so POL-RD-08(b) is met. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause — a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge it.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the extra-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: her deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, nowhere near the four-or-more claims with one-or-fewer substantiated combination that clause names. Her claim therefore stands on the trace without more, and nothing on her profile may be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The chat log shows the re-route was the driver's own proposal, not a rider instruction: at 20:38:12 he wrote 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', and the rider's only reply at 20:38:55 was 'ok but not too long ah'. That reply is not a rider instruction, names no road and no place, and carries a null waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test — that the vehicle passed within 200 m of a requested waypoint or travelled a requested road — cannot be run on this record and the clause exonerates nothing. A bare assent cannot convert the driver's own choice of a 34.17 km corridor into a rider-requested detour; and the rider's express qualification, 'not too long', is inconsistent with 7.07 km of extra distance on a 27.1 km route.

Even taking the driver's PIE advisory at its highest, POL-RD-03 caps the exoneration it can buy. The justified excess is min(measured 7.07 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 30.1 km - booked optimal 27.1 km) + 1.00 km) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, leaving 2.17 km of this trip's excess that no closure explains and that is refundable under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route. The cap bites hardest because the driver's own trace shows 34.17 km, which is 4.07 km longer than the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative the advisory made available: the mileage beyond the lawful alternative is the driver's choice, not the accident's.

The second advisory the driver invokes, ADV-20260716-055, records intersects_route: false — it describes a breakdown on the CTE towards SLE after Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, a corridor the optimal PIE route never uses. POL-RD-03 is explicit that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses does not exonerate anything, and a CTE incident cannot account for a route that ran down the ECP, the MCE and the AYE.

No amended endpoint exists on this record: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, no amended optimal distance or duration is stored, and there is no original pickup or dropoff. POL-RD-05 therefore does not open, no relocation re-quote displaces the baseline, and the comparator for POL-RD-01 remains the booked 27.1 km optimal between the booked Tampines Hub and one-north endpoints.

The fare model on this trip is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and does not close off a distance-and-time refund: the rider was billed by the meter on distance and time, and POL-RD-02 is the clause that runs.

On the closure-adjusted optimal route of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes — the booked 27.1 km plus the 4.90 km justified excess, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 minutes — the POL-RD-02 recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 39.828. The rider's refund is the charged 43.41 less 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total: PARTIAL_REFUND, with charged_total, recomputed_fare and refund stated on separate lines.

In the alternative, if the judge finds POL-RD-03(c) unmet — that the record does not show the driver's ECP/MCE/AYE route leaving the optimal corridor before the affected PIE segment and rejoining it after — then no part of the excess is exonerated and the POL-RD-02 computation runs on the booked optimal: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 27.1 + 0.28 x 34.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 34.445, refund 43.41 - 34.445 = 8.965, rounded up to SGD 9.00. On either footing the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND, not nothing.

This charge is live and unreversed: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION leaves the present payment state exactly as it is, which on a rider-filed dispute means the rider keeps carrying the disputed charge; the only outcomes that give this rider anything are the refund outcomes, and on this record the supported one is PARTIAL_REFUND.

ruling.explanation:
Decision on trip TRP-00104 (Tampines Hub to one-north), for both parties.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS. The GPS trace measures 34.17 km and that is the figure that governs the threshold test (POL-RD-01; the trip record's 34.2 km is a rounded copy and may not be cited). The booked optimal route was 27.1 km. The excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own measurement. It does not reach either materiality marker (50% or 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and in any event the driver's trailing-90-day record is 1 flag in 288 completed trips, far below the pattern thresholds, so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral can follow. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not substituted. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (283 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-07's corroboration rule and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route are not open, and the excess is measured directly.

THE DRIVER'S EXONERATION. POL-RD-03 applies. LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 (HIGH severity, two of three lanes blocked) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit, which is the corridor the optimal route uses, and its 20:02-21:35 window overlaps the trip; the route left that corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it. The driver was right to avoid the accident and is not fined for it. But the exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The driver's own trace, 34.17 km, is 4.07 km longer than the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative the advisory made available; that mileage is the driver's choice, not the accident's. The second advisory (ADV-20260716-055, CTE towards SLE, intersects_route false) exonerates nothing: it covers a corridor the optimal route never uses.

THE REFUND. The closure-adjusted optimal is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 to 40.1 minutes. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 charged_total - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the fare, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Charged_total 43.41, recomputed_fare 39.828 and refund 3.60 are the three lines.

ON THE DRIVER'S "NO ACTION" ARGUMENT. I do not accept that the 2.17 km residue fails POL-RD-01 and leaves the whole charge standing. POL-RD-03 states expressly that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and IS refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 directs its computation onto the adjusted route wherever POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess. The 2.17 km is the part no closure explains, and it is refunded. The driver's fallback figure of a 3.60 ceiling is therefore right; his primary request that nothing be refunded is not.

ON THE RIDER'S ALTERNATIVE FIGURE. The SGD 9.00 computed on the unadjusted 27.1 km / 34.0 min baseline is not available: the POL-RD-03 exoneration is made out on the cited advisory, its window and the route geometry, so the refund runs on the adjusted baseline, not the booked one. The rider's sense that 43.41 is about 14.00 more than usual is not the measure the policy uses.

OTHER CLAUSES. POL-RD-04 does not apply: the reroute was the driver's own proposal ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'); the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' is not an instruction naming a road or place, and waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested detour is made out and no excess is excluded on that ground. POL-RD-05 does not open (no amended pickup or dropoff, no amended optimal stored). POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund route is not closed. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00, and there is no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral. POL-RD-08 is satisfied on both sides as described, and the rider's profile does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule. The charge is live (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued 0.00).

Both parties' profiles were used only to weight credibility; no context-only field (ratings, acceptance rate, account age, lifetime counters, prior disputes) has been used to decide anything about this trip.

No mandatory escalation applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing or inapplicable artifact, and the refund is well within the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling. Confidence 0.9, the cap being the full weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
